title: Application projections and surface composition
behavioral_concerns: Adapter-neutral performance DTOs expose bounded sample-free status, target qualification, limit provenance, and evidence metadata.
Dashboard, TUI, and web composition receive the same effective performance limits and sources.
Disabled or missing policy remains side-effect free and presentation fixtures cover every supported state.
Projection and error mapping sanitize hostile text and omit raw private evidence.
Status distinguishes performance attempt identity, durable run identity, operational lifecycle, freshness, and product outcome.

evidence.summary: The summary helper calls the raw performance projection, while only the public PerformanceStatus method consults RunUseCases to populate operational lifecycle and cancellation state.
PerformanceResult returns a plain fmt.Errorf when status.Result is nil; the web mapper's performance branch requires PerformanceUseCaseError.

theories.claim: Sprint summary, TUI, and web performance projections omit operational lifecycle and cancellation state even when a durable run exists.
theories.basis: qa-v1-block-78e13c26eb8ae322452c9951 calls performanceStatusProjection directly for summaries; qa-v1-block-c1bc237cbe63b9df34c97ed7 embeds that summary into dashboard composition; qa-v1-block-95f9f726d965e7685184fba7 serves the embedded summary from the performance endpoint.
theories.verification_surface: internal/app/sprint_usecases.go performanceSummaryForSprint, PerformanceStatus, and SprintSummaries; internal/web/handlers.go api_sprint_performance; internal/tui/model.go performance navigation.
theories.confirmation_condition: A state with a non-empty operation run ID and an inspectable durable lifecycle produces an empty operational_lifecycle or cancellation_state through SprintSummaries or api_sprint_performance while direct PerformanceStatus supplies those fields.
theories.refutation_condition: Sprint summary composition enriches the projection from the durable run manager, or all consuming adapters call the enriched PerformanceStatus use case instead of the raw projection.
theories.inconclusive_condition: The durable lifecycle enrichment or Sprint query implementation differs outside the cited excerpts such that the summary is enriched before presentation.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Use a read-only fixture containing a performance correlation run ID and a fake RunUseCases snapshot, then compare direct PerformanceStatus with SprintSummaries and the mapped web response without starting runtime work.

theories.claim: PerformanceResult returns an unclassified raw error when no terminal result exists, bypassing performance-specific transport error mapping.
theories.basis: qa-v1-block-35e4c5fcc8d7288b70a46a1e introduces the adapter-neutral PerformanceResult boundary; qa-v1-block-95f9f726d965e7685184fba7 forwards its error to handleQueryError; qa-v1-block-d5ce194480a423a58e7143af only applies performance HTTP classification to PerformanceUseCaseError values; qa-v1-block-307234c6bfff53948b392930 requires classified, context-preserving boundary errors.
theories.verification_surface: internal/app/sprint_usecases.go PerformanceResult and mapPerformanceUseCaseError; internal/web/handlers.go performance-result dispatch and handleQueryError.
theories.confirmation_condition: Calling PerformanceResult for a valid nonterminal attempt returns the raw "performance result is unavailable" error, AsPerformanceUseCaseError returns false, and the web route falls through to generic error handling.
theories.refutation_condition: The unavailable-result branch wraps the error through mapPerformanceUseCaseError or another recognized typed error before returning.
theories.inconclusive_condition: An outer boundary not shown in the cited route always classifies this raw error before handleQueryError receives it.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Invoke the read-only PerformanceResult use case with a fake status lacking Result, assert the returned error type, and pass it through the web error mapper without executing commands or writing state.

Test internal/app/qa_investigator_6fe849fce7fe_test.go:
package app

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

func TestQAInvestigator_6fe849fce7fe(t *testing.T) {
	// Control: the production classifier produces the typed shape consumed by
	// performance-specific transport mapping.
	control := mapPerformanceUseCaseError("performance.result", errors.New("performance result is unavailable"))
	typedControl, ok := AsPerformanceUseCaseError(control)
	if !ok || typedControl.Code != "performance.persistence_unavailable" || typedControl.Category != "persistence" {
		t.Fatalf("control performance mapping = %#v, typed=%t", control, ok)
	}

	root := initializedWorkspace(t)
	projectRoot := filepath.Join(root, "projects", "alpha")
	writeFixtureFileContent(t, projectRoot, "# Project Index\n\n## Performance Policy\n\n- **Mode:** disabled\n", "project-index.md")
	writeFixtureFileContent(t, filepath.Join(projectRoot, "sprints", "01-ready"), "# Requirements\n\nNo performance targets are enabled.\n", "requirements.md")

	_, err := (dashboardUseCases{root: root, readOnly: true}).PerformanceResult(context.Background(), PerformanceRequest{Project: "alpha", Sprint: "01-ready"})
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected a nonterminal performance result to be unavailable")
	}
	if _, ok := AsPerformanceUseCaseError(err); !ok {
		t.Fatalf("ULTRAPLAN_QA_PREDICTED_FAILURE:TestQAInvestigator_6fe849fce7fe assertion=Assert that the error is not recognized as a PerformanceUseCaseError and receives generic mapping.")
	}
}
